page: Microsoft Azure FX24ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 504.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching the top 25% and top 10% tiers respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform in the top 25% tier. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core, fall within the middle 50% average. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is high at 2073.56 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score registers in the bottom 25% tier, indicating a potential bottleneck under specific memory-access patterns.

The FX24ms_v2 is designed for memory-heavy workloads that require high single-core clock speeds, such as relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers, and text processing pipelines. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions enables efficient small-model LLM inference, as evidenced by top-tier text generation speeds of 420.68 tokens/sec for a 135M model. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 504 GB RAM paired with 24 dedicated vCPUs provides a specialized hardware profile that reduces the need to over-provision compute cores solely to obtain massive memory capacity.
